01 — SERVICES FOR RESEARCHERS

Order the computation. Get results you can publish.

Every engagement is scoped in writing before work starts — systems, parameters, deliverables and timeline — so the report you receive matches the quotation you approved. Tap a service for exactly what's included.

WHAT YOU RECEIVE

  • Prepared receptor and ligand structures (cleaned, protonated, energy-minimised)
  • Docked poses with binding affinities and ranked scores
  • Interaction analysis — hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic contacts, key residues
  • Publication-ready interaction figures and a written interpretation
  • All raw output files, so your reviewers can verify every number

WHY SIMULATE AT ALL?

A docking score is a snapshot.
Dynamics is the film.

Docking tells you a ligand can fit. An MD simulation tells you whether it stays bound, which residues hold it, and when the complex breathes or falls apart. That difference is what reviewers ask about — and what BioInfoX reports, frame by frame:

  • Stability, quantified — RMSD and RMSF profiles across the full trajectory, not a single frame.
  • Interactions over time — hydrogen-bond occupancy and contact maps, so claims survive peer review.
  • Reproducibility — replicas and controls (apo, standard-drug) run alongside your system.
  • Everything handed over — trajectories, topologies and analysis files are yours to keep and re-analyse.
02 — HOW IT WORKS

From first email to final files, in four steps

No portals, no ticket numbers. You describe the project, approve a written scope, and receive files you can verify.

STEP 1

Describe the project

Email your target, ligands or idea — PDB IDs, sequences, papers, even a rough sketch of the study. Use the quote builder below to structure it.

STEP 2

Approve the scope

You get a written quotation: exact systems, simulation lengths, replicas, deliverables, price and completion time. Nothing runs until you say yes.

STEP 3

Computation & analysis

Systems are prepared, equilibrated and run. Progress updates come by email, and questions are answered by the researcher doing the work.

STEP 4

Report & raw files

You receive the written report, publication-ready figures and the complete raw data — trajectories, inputs and outputs — for your records.

03 — THE RESEARCHER BEHIND BIOINFOX

One website, because it's one person doing both.

BioInfoX is the practice of Muhammad Nouman Majeed — bioinformatician and biotechnology researcher working in in silico drug and vaccine design. The same hands that run client simulations publish the research, teach the trainings, and answer your emails.

His work centres on molecular docking and GROMACS molecular dynamics — testing, in the computer, whether a candidate drug or vaccine construct behaves the way the hypothesis says it should, before anyone spends on the wet lab.

04 — TRAINING

Or learn to run it yourself

BioInfoX training is built for students and researchers who need the skill, not a certificate to frame. Sessions are live, online, and taught in English, Urdu or Punjabi.

COURSE A

Molecular docking, hands-on

Structure preparation, grid setup, docking runs and interaction analysis — practised on a real target from your own field, with the mistakes beginners make explained before you make them in your thesis.

COURSE B

GROMACS MD, start to analysis

The full workflow: topology, solvation, equilibration, production runs, and the RMSD / RMSF / hydrogen-bond analysis that turns a trajectory into a results section.

WITH ANY ORDER

Training bundled with your project

Add training to a docking, MD or DFT order and learn on your own systems — so when the report arrives, you can explain every figure in your viva or review meeting.

06 — QUESTIONS

Before you ask

For docking: a target (PDB ID or file) and your ligands (names, SMILES or files). For MD: a docked complex, or ask for docking first. For DFT: the structures. If you're not sure what you have, email what exists — part of the job is telling you what's missing.
By scope: number of systems, simulation length, replicas and analysis depth. DFT has a per-structure rate (recently PKR 2,500 per calculation on BioInfoX invoices). Everything else is priced in a written quotation you approve before work begins — the figure in the quote is the figure you pay.
A written report with methods, results and publication-ready figures — plus the complete raw data (trajectories, topology, input and output files). The raw files matter: they let you, your supervisor or a reviewer re-check any number in the report.
Yes — that's the training side of BioInfoX. Live online sessions cover docking, GROMACS and DFT, taught in English, Urdu or Punjabi, and can be bundled with a service order so you practise on your own project.
Muhammad Nouman Majeed — founder of BioInfoX, Master's in Biotechnology, ~40 publications and 196 citations, Best Research Student Award (University of Okara, 2024). There is no hand-off to an anonymous freelancer; the person you email is the person who runs your simulation.
Payment terms are agreed in the quotation — project work is commonly split, with part in advance and the balance on delivery. BioInfoX operates as BioInfoX SMC Private Limited, Pakistan, and invoices are issued for orders.
